props.gloss_en: apparently, as long as its prohibition is not abrogated [by designating a lamb], the doubtful firstborn donkey is forbidden in benefit
whose is the mishna? R' Yehuda's
a firstborn donkey is forbidden in benefit
and R' Shimon permits [benefit from it]
Ulla: is there anything that requires redemption and is permitted [before it]?
a firstborn son requires redemption and is permitted
rather: is there anything the Torah was particular to redeem with a lamb and is permitted [before it]?
Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef redeemed [a firstborn donkey] with boiled vegetables at its value
R' Yehuda: [one who betrothed with maaser sheni] intentionally -- has betrothed
R' Elazar: the woman knows maaser sheni is not desacralized through her, and goes up and eats it in Jerusalem
with a firstborn donkey too she is betrothed: she knows it carries a prohibition, redeems it with a lamb, and is betrothed with the difference
Ulla: is there anything whose redemption is permitted while it is forbidden?
alternatively: R' Yehuda and R' Shimon dispute over this verse
R' Yehuda: 'you shall not work with the firstborn of YOUR ox' -- but you may work with one that is yours and others'
R' Yehuda: 'nor shear the firstborn of YOUR flock' -- but you may shear one that is yours and others'
R' Shimon: 'the firstborn of your OX' -- but you may work with a firstborn son
R' Shimon: 'the firstborn of your FLOCK' -- but you may shear a firstborn donkey
rather, all agree 'your ox' comes to exclude a firstborn son
where they disagree is over 'your flock'
R' Yehuda: an animal owned in partnership with a gentile is subject to firstborn status
[for R' Yehuda] the verse was needed to permit shearing and work [in the gentile-partnership firstborn]
R' Shimon: an animal owned in partnership with a gentile is exempt from firstborn status
[for R' Shimon] no verse was needed for shearing and work; the verse was needed for the firstborn donkey
R' Shimon concedes that after its neck is broken it is forbidden [in benefit]
orla, vineyard kilayim, the ox to be stoned, the heifer, the leper's birds, the firstborn donkey and meat in milk are all susceptible to food-impurity
R' Shimon: none of them is susceptible to food-impurity
and R' Shimon concedes that meat in milk is susceptible to food-impurity
R' Shimon's reason: since it had a time of fitness
R' Yochanan: R' Shimon's source is 'of all the food which may be eaten' (Lev 11:34)
R' Yochanan's criterion: food you can feed to others is called food; what you cannot feed to others is not called food
R' Shimon (via R' Shimon b. Yehuda): meat in milk is forbidden to eat and permitted in benefit -- 'holy' here (Deut 14:21) and 'holy' there (Ex 22:30)
the Sages before Rav Sheshet: [the Rabbis make it susceptible] because its prohibition is its designation [as food]
the mishna: of thirteen things said of the carcass of a pure bird, one is that it needs intent and needs no wetting
the mishna: the carcass of an impure animal anywhere, and the carcass of a pure bird and forbidden fat in the villages, need intent and need no wetting
the mishna: the carcass of a pure animal anywhere, and a pure bird's carcass and fat in the markets, need neither intent nor wetting -- hence an impure animal needs intent
R' Shimon: even the camel, hare, hyrax and pig need neither intent nor wetting -- since they have signs of purity
Rava: all agree we do not say its prohibition is its designation; and if its neck was broken -- indeed [it is not susceptible]
Rava: the baraita's firstborn donkey is one slaughtered to practise on, and [the tannaim] dispute as Nimos and R' Eliezer do
Nimos: one who slaughters a crow to practise on -- its blood renders [food] susceptible
R' Eliezer: the blood of slaughter always renders susceptible
R' Eliezer says what the first tanna says! rather, isn't issuro chishuvo the difference between them?
the first tanna: its blood renders other things susceptible, but the crow itself needs intent
R' Eliezer: the blood always renders susceptible, and even the crow itself needs no intent
perhaps R' Eliezer's reason there is that a crow differs, having some signs of purity
the baraita: if he will not redeem it he breaks its neck from behind with a cleaver and buries it, and it is forbidden in benefit -- R' Yehuda; R' Shimon permits
the וערפתו baraita follows R' Yehuda (eliminated at 10b.17, restored by Safra at 10b.18)
the וערפתו baraita follows R' Shimon
Levi's baraita: he caused the priest a loss, therefore his own money is lost
Levi's baraita follows R' Yehuda (the loss is the difference)
Levi's baraita follows R' Shimon
it is still in dispute: R' Shimon permits even after its neck is broken
one who betroths with a firstborn donkey -- she is not betrothed
Rabba bar Avuha (via Rav Nachman, in the איכא דמתני version): [the mishna speaks of] after the neck is broken, and it is everyone's view
Rav (via Rabba bar Avuha, in the איכא דאמרי version): it is R' Yehuda's, where the donkey is worth only a shekel, and he holds with R' Yosei bar Yehuda
the baraita: 'you shall redeem' -- redeem at once, redeem with any amount
R' Yosei bar Yehuda: no redemption is less than a shekel
Rava: [RYBY's shekel] is from 'and all your valuations shall be by the shekel of the Sanctuary' (Lev 27:25)
Rava's criterion: all valuations you assess shall not be less than a shekel
and the Rabbis: that verse is written of [valuations by] means
how much? Rav Yosef: even a lean lamb worth a danka
the mishna (9a), cited by Rava: [he may give] a large or a small [lamb]
R' Tarfon: they said -- the generous with a sela, the miserly with a shekel, the middling with a regia
Rava: the halakha is a regia
how much is a regia? three zuz -- close to this and close to that
Reish Lakish: one who has a firstborn donkey and no lamb to redeem it redeems it at its value
whose view is it? not R' Yehuda's, who says the Torah was particular about a lamb -- R' Shimon's (Rav Acha's version)
Ravina: between R' Yehuda and R' Shimon the halakha is R' Yehuda, and the tanna taught us an anonymous mishna like R' Yehuda
Ravina: rather, [Reish Lakish's rule holds] even according to R' Yehuda
Ravina: it should not be stricter than hekdesh; the Torah said 'with a lamb' not to be strict with him but to be lenient
Rav Huna: one who redeems another's firstborn donkey -- it is redeemed
the redeemed donkey belongs to the owner (for R' Shimon without question; for R' Yehuda as the ת"ש resolves)
the baraita: one who steals another's firstborn donkey pays double to the owner -- though he has no [right] now, he has afterwards

תא שמע: נבלת בהמה טמאה בכל מקום ... צריכים מחשבה; ואי אמרת איסורו חישובו, למה לי מחשבה?

תא שמע: נבלת בהמה טהורה ... אינן צריכין מחשבה -- הא טמאה בעיא מחשבה; וכי תימא הא מני רבי שמעון -- הא מדסיפא רבי שמעון, רישא לאו רבי שמעון (10a.11): the anticipated answer is closed off, so the objection stands
ממאי? דילמא טעמא דרבי אליעזר התם דשאני עורב, הואיל ויש בו סימני טהרה; ומנלן דסימני טהרה מילתא היא? דקתני ... (10b.7); וכי תימא מאי איריא להתלמד ... אין הכי נמי, ומשום נימוס (10b.8)
איתיביה: לא רצה לפדותו עורפו ... וקוברו, ואסור בהנאה, דברי רבי יהודה, ורבי שמעון מתיר

answered_by.gloss_en: אימא: ומחיים אסור בהנאה (10b.10); והא מדסיפא מחיים, רישא לאו מחיים (10b.11-12) -- רישא וסיפא מחיים: רישא בהנאת דמיו, סיפא בהנאת גופו (10b.13). The intermediate counter-and-reply attacks an answer, which the format cannot hold (header)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: כאן בבא לימלך, כאן בעושה מעצמו

objections.gloss_en: רבינא קשיא ליה: רבי יהודה ורבי שמעון הלכה כרבי יהודה, וסתם לן תנא כרבי יהודה, ואת אמרת הלכה כרבי שמעון?! -- replaced by אלא, אפילו תימא רבי יהודה (11a.10)
